A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same width/LMC study. Their text, equations, figures and appendices support reliable comparison despite the revised title and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-merging accuracy/loss experiments and layerwise activation analyses on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds flatness, activation-norm, optimizer and architectural experiments.

M1.justification: Width expansion, weight interpolation, BatchNorm recalibration, temperature calibration and the LEWC construction are retained. The added optimizer and architecture studies test the existing approach without introducing a new merging procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate standard image classification on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100. The new controls reuse these datasets and tasks; CIFAR-100 was already included in v1 Appendix E.1.

E2.justification: v2 adds WM to the active-neuron-overlap analysis, previously reported only without permutations (Figure 22 versus Figure 6). Appendix F.10 also compares Sophia against the existing first-order optimizers. The main merging comparators are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include Gaussian parameter perturbations normalized to inter-model distance, a weight-decay sweep from 0 to 0.003, Sophia with retained training hyperparameters, and MLP variants with skip connections or BatchNorm. The original training settings and 20%/80% calibration/evaluation split remain.

E4.justification: Appendices D and F add flatness controls, direct activation-norm measurements, permutation-dependent neuron overlap, broader weight-decay sensitivity, and optimizer/architecture ablations. The weak-decay LEWC analysis itself is retained from v1 Appendix E.5/Figure 15 and moved into v2 Section 5.4/Figure 10.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three independent merges and mean/standard-deviation reporting in Section 3.1. Additional plots and table entries continue uncertainty reporting without specifying changed run counts, seed practices, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds numerical barriers and outcomes for the new controls, including exponential norm decay in MLPs but not the BatchNorm architectures, and generally larger barriers under Sophia. Table 1 reports VGG-11 calibrated loss barriers of 0.066 ± 0.054 without permutations and 0.177 ± 0.039 with WM; these are within-version comparisons, not improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The principal definitions, theorems and proofs are retained, with proofs relocated from Appendix D to E. In the proof of Theorem 5.4, one tail-bound step changes t^2/K to t^2/K^2, a local mathematical correction.

C1.justification: The central claims remain permutation-free LMC through sufficient width and calibration, its explanation through LEWC, and the importance of low-rank weights. The added conclusion clarifies the work's analytical purpose without materially changing these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 expands the LLFC/LEWC distinction and argues that random-direction flatness alone cannot explain LMC. It explicitly qualifies the low-rank-to-sparsity connection and discusses BatchNorm's effect on norm decay and the limitations of unretuned Sophia settings.

D1.justification: New sections document perturbation normalization, retention of training hyperparameters for Sophia, and how skip connections are inserted into MLPs. Appendix B's existing hardware, software, training details and implementation links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds a focused width/loss-landscape discussion citing Nguyen (2021), Simsek et al. (2021), Liang et al. (2018), Li et al. (2022) and Kim et al. (2025). Sophia's reference and a fuller comparison with Zhou et al.'s LLFC are also added, while the central positioning remains.

P1.justification: The title, affiliations, conference header and selected introductory/concluding paragraphs are edited. ReLU statistics receive more accurate second-moment terminology, and the weak-decay discussion moves into the main text. The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 1 and numerous multi-panel figures for the new analyses. Existing plots are recolored and reformatted, including Figure 1's accuracy range changing from 0–100 to 50–100. The old appendix Figure 15 becomes main-text Figure 10.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the direct norm-decay measurements and optimizer/architecture controls strengthen the mechanism's empirical assessment, while the sparsity qualification improves precision. Reporting inconsistencies limit the gain: F.9 reverses Figure 23's weight-decay trend, and Figure 12 labels lambda from 1–11 although Appendix D specifies 0–1.
